question: Must this fix cover endpoint/CDN and trusted-network substitution of both Node release responses, or should the linked report be narrowed to corruption and archive-only replacement?
rationale: Unsigned same-origin checksum comparison cannot authenticate the digest when the attacker controls both responses, while signed verification requires a deliberate trusted-key and rotation policy.

options.title: Cover broader substitution
options.body: Verify signed Node checksum metadata against a pinned, reviewed release-key set and define how trusted keys are updated.

options.title: Narrow the threat model
options.body: Retain unsigned checksum comparison but explicitly exclude attackers able to replace the checksum-manifest response.

recommendation.title: Cover broader substitution
recommendation.body: Verify signed Node checksum metadata against a pinned, reviewed release-key set and define how trusted keys are updated.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties this person to both the affected hydration implementation and the security-scope language defining the boundary.
